author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader narrows the veterinarian directory to one specialty through the address
summary: Both forms of the veterinarian directory, the paged page and the machine-readable document, can be narrowed to the veterinarians holding one named specialty, carried in the address alone. Matching is on the whole name, ignoring letter case. A specialty nobody holds yields an empty list, and a blank name is ignored.
acceptance_criteria: GET /vets.html?specialty=<name> lists only the veterinarians holding that specialty, and pagination applies to the filtered list (PRD REQ-VET-003).
On a filtered /vets.html page, every pagination link carries the specialty parameter, so each linked page stays filtered to the same specialty.
GET /vets?specialty=<name> returns the machine-readable document containing only the veterinarians holding that specialty.
On both surfaces, matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive: a letter-case variant of a held specialty matches; a prefix of a specialty name matches no veterinarian.
On both surfaces, a specialty that no veterinarian holds yields HTTP 200 with the normal page or document and an empty veterinarian list.
On both surfaces, an empty or whitespace-only specialty value behaves exactly as if the parameter were absent.
Without the parameter both surfaces behave as today: the paged HTML directory (REQ-VET-001) and the full machine-readable list in one document (REQ-VET-004).
A veterinarian holding several specialties appears once in a filtered result and is still shown with every specialty they hold (PRD Veterinarian directory edge case 2).
A veterinarian holding no specialty never matches a filter, including a value equal to the word the page shows for having none (PRD Veterinarian directory edge case 3).
non_goals: Any form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing a specialty on either surface. Owner decision: the filter is a URL contract only, and a visible control may come as a follow-up request.
Free-text veterinarian search, and filtering by any attribute other than specialty. NG-9 as narrowed still excludes free-text search; other attributes were not requested.
Filtering by more than one specialty at once.
New user-facing wording, such as a notice that the list is filtered or that no veterinarian matched. A no-match result is the normal page or document with an empty list.
Any change to unfiltered behavior on either surface, including paging the machine-readable document.
Pinning whether spaces around a non-blank specialty value are disregarded. This stays an open question in the PRD, and no test fixes either behavior.
notes: Requirement shape (my decision): REQ-VET-003 is the narrowing capability across both surfaces. REQ-VET-004 is the fresh requirement for the reinstated machine-readable directory (intake decision 2). REQ-VET-002 stays in Superseded, now pointing to REQ-VET-004. REQ-VET-004's unfiltered behavior already ships, so it gets no separate slice; the unchanged-behavior criterion here covers it. NG-9 narrowed per intake decision 1 and recorded in docs/adr/2026-09-13-non-goal-narrow-veterinarian-search.md. For system-design-expert: (a) docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for that ADR, which is outside my write scope; (b) system-design.md is now stale in three places: the Known Defects row saying the machine-readable route serves no requirement and is pending removal, the Implements column for Vets/VetController, and the overview line saying there is no JSON API; (c) the case-insensitive match must hold on every supported database, which is the REQ-OWN-002 edge case 3 precedent. Open questions recorded in the PRD and deliberately left open: name filtering under NG-9, spaces around a non-blank value, multi-specialty filtering, a visible control.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice stays inside the vet feature package (system-design.md § Package Structure), with no new module, type, or cross-package edge. VetRepository gains one narrowed read. VetController's two existing routes gain an optional specialty request parameter, and the template's pagination links carry it. The new ground is two cross-slice decisions, now recorded. (1) Case-insensitive matching is done in the query, applying one case function to both sides of a whole-name equality, never through the column's collation. The three vendor schemas disagree on case: the specialty column is case-sensitive under H2 and PostgreSQL. Owner search's dependence on the column is the recorded PostgreSQL defect (ADR 2026-09-13-case-insensitive-matching-in-the-query; § Persistence). (2) The narrowed read is uncached, because the vet cache has no size limit and a key taken from caller text would grow it without bound (ADR 2026-09-13-uncached-reads-keyed-by-caller-text; § Contracts VetRepository row; § Threat Model). Normalizing a blank value to absent is binding by the Web controller row of architecture-principles.md § pattern catalog, so it sits in the controller and is tested at the web level (testing-principles.md § Test Pyramid). The unfiltered branch of both handlers calls the existing cached reads unchanged. Basis: the IDE oracle is not connected. Covering code was resolved by reading VetController, VetRepository, Vet, Vets, CacheConfiguration, vetList.html, and the three vendor schema.sql files, plus a grep for @Query in src/main/java. That is the weaker basis.
integration_points: VetRepository gains one narrowed read taking the specialty name and a Pageable and returning a Page of Vet: an explicitly parameterized JPQL @Query, @Transactional(readOnly = true) like its siblings, and no @Cacheable. The HTML route passes the existing page request (same local page size as the unfiltered helper). The machine-readable route passes Pageable.unpaged(), so one query text serves both surfaces.

The match is an existence test (or DISTINCT) over v.specialties with lower(s.name) = lower(:specialty), or the equivalent derived IgnoreCase form, which folds both sides in SQL. It is never LIKE or a StartingWith form, and never a fetch join on the filtered association.

VetController, both handlers: bind @RequestParam(required = false) String specialty. A null or isBlank() value takes the existing unfiltered path unchanged. A non-blank value takes the narrowed read. The HTML handler exposes the specialty to the model only on the narrowed path, and the machine-readable handler wraps the narrowed list in the existing Vets wrapper.

vetList.html: every pagination link carries specialty as a Thymeleaf link-expression parameter, e.g. @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}. On the unfiltered page the links stay free of the parameter.

Binding target, both routes: the request-scoped scalar String request parameter only. No command object, @ModelAttribute, Vet, or Specialty is bound, so there is no data binder whose identifier disallow list the new parameter could bypass (security-principles.md § Realization, mass assignment row).

Double, repository boundary, semantic tests (whole-name, case, empty result, several specialties once, no specialty, blank ignored, both surfaces narrowed): a real implementation. Use @SpringBootTest plus @AutoConfigureMockMvc in the new VetDirectoryFilterIntegrationTests, driving the real VetRepository against the seeded H2 database (testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy, real I/O for integration). A stubbed repository would only prove the stub. The seed covers every case: radiology held by two vets, a vet holding dentistry and surgery, a vet holding none, six vets in total.

Double, repository boundary, theVetDirectoryPaginationShouldKeepTheSpecialtyFilter only: a framework stub, the existing @MockitoBean VetRepository in VetControllerTests (@WebMvcTest), returning a multi-page Page from the narrowed read. The reason neither alternative fits: the seed holds at most two vets per specialty, below the page size, and VetRepository has no write path. Rows inserted for a test would also leak into the unbounded shared vets cache through any unfiltered read.
Double, HTTP transport: MockMvc for all web-level tests (the one sanctioned mock, testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy).

Vendor check: add one repository-level assertion each to MySqlIntegrationTests and PostgresIntegrationTests. A letter-case variant of a seeded specialty (e.g. RADIOLOGY) returns that specialty's holders. They run when Docker is present and cover the every-vendor requirement that the H2 default suite cannot see (ADR 2026-09-13-case-insensitive-matching-in-the-query, Context).

patterns.description: A paged search handler normalizes its request value before the query: null means broadest, and the value is stripped. The vet handlers normalize a blank specialty to absent the same way, at the web layer.
A paged Spring Data read taking a caller value and a Pageable and returning a Page. The narrowed vet read takes the same shape, minus the prefix semantics.
An existing explicit @Query JPQL read. Its form is the parameterized-query precedent in this codebase.
findPaginated holds the local page size and PageRequest construction. The narrowed path reuses it rather than declaring a second size.

risks.risk: Relying on column collation makes the match case-sensitive under H2 and PostgreSQL, since both specialty columns are case-sensitive. Folding only the Java side ties correctness to stored names staying lower-case.
risks.mitigation: Fold both operands inside the query. The H2 suite then exercises the same comparison every vendor runs, and the vendor integration tests assert a case variant (ADR 2026-09-13-case-insensitive-matching-in-the-query; system-design.md § Persistence).

risks.risk: A pattern match (LIKE or StartingWith) would let a prefix, or a % or _ in the caller's value, match veterinarians.
risks.mitigation: Whole-name equality only (same ADR, Decision). theSpecialtyFilterShouldMatchTheWholeNameIgnoringCase asserts that a prefix matches no one.

risks.risk: A plain join over the many-to-many can return a veterinarian twice. H2's vet_specialties has no unique (vet_id, specialty_id) constraint. A fetch join filtered on the specialty would also truncate the veterinarian's specialties to the matched one.
risks.mitigation: Use an existence subquery (or DISTINCT with its derived count) and leave the eager specialties collection unfiltered (system-design.md § Contracts, invariants paragraph). The several-specialties test asserts one row carrying both specialties.

risks.risk: Caching the narrowed read would key the unbounded vets cache on caller text, giving remote memory exhaustion.
risks.mitigation: No @Cacheable on the narrowed read (ADR 2026-09-13-uncached-reads-keyed-by-caller-text; system-design.md § Threat Model, memory exhaustion row).

risks.risk: Carrying the specialty into links through the template's current __${...}__ preprocessing, or through string-built href text, would evaluate or splice caller text into a template expression.
risks.mitigation: Pass it only as a link-expression parameter, which the engine URL-encodes. The existing integer page preprocessing may stay or move to parameters (system-design.md § Threat Model, template expression injection row; security-principles.md § Realization, cross-site scripting row).
A bound :specialty parameter in a Spring Data query only, with no concatenation (security-principles.md § Realization, injection into data access row).

risks.risk: Changing the unfiltered path on either surface would breach the prd-entry non-goal and REQ-VET-001 and REQ-VET-004.
risks.mitigation: The unfiltered branch calls the existing findAll(Pageable) and findAll() unchanged, still cached (system-design.md § Contracts, VetRepository row). Existing VetControllerTests stay green, and theSpecialtyFilterShouldBeIgnoredWhenBlank asserts the whole directory.

risks.risk: A test that inserts veterinarians in a full-context test pollutes the shared cache across tests. The rows roll back but cached unfiltered results do not.
risks.mitigation: Semantic tests use the seed only. The one multi-page case uses the web-slice stub named in integration_points (system-design.md § Open Questions from the Survey, item 5).

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; nothing to judge. Doc writes this dispatch: system-design.md (provenance header clause, Overview machine-readable line, Contracts invariants and the Vet, Specialty, Vets, VetRepository, VetController, and CacheConfiguration rows with REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004, § Persistence case-folding paragraph, Security Context inputs and outputs, two designed Threat Model rows, SQL injection row made count-free, the stale Known Defects row for the machine-readable route removed). Two new ADRs, plus three index rows in docs/adr/README.md, including the product expert's non-goal ADR (requested in the prd-entry notes). I did not write the non-goal ADR and do not claim its path. Open question left open by design: whether spaces around a non-blank value are disregarded. The implementation may pass the value through unchanged or stripped, and no test pins either. Brief gap for the owner of security-principles.md, which is outside my write scope: § Realization has no row for server-side template expression injection. The cross-site scripting row is the nearest, and the Threat Model row now carries the control. The design-validation skill asks a triage to write a new principle to the owning brief, but this agent's write scope excludes the principle briefs. That contradiction is surfaced here, not resolved.

findings.description: Each of the five pagination `<a th:href>` sites repeats the same `${filtered} ? @{/vets.html(page=…,specialty=${specialty})} : @{/vets.html(page=…)}` ternary, differing only in the page value. `th:with="filtered=…"` factors the boolean but not the href construction itself — the checklist's 'conditional repeated across sibling sites' duplication rule (code-quality-review skill, Control Flow) still applies to the five link expressions.
findings.fix: Extract a Thymeleaf fragment (e.g. `th:fragment="pageLink(page)"`) that builds the href once from `page` and the enclosing `specialty` model attribute, and reference it (`th:replace`/`th:insert`) from all five call sites, so the specialty-vs-unfiltered branching is written once.

approved_aspects: VetController's narrowing normalizes a blank specialty to absent at the web layer via `narrowsTheDirectory`/`StringUtils.hasText`, matching the Web controller row's placement doctrine recorded in the design-block (system-design.md, verified by reading src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet/VetController.java:43-88 in the diff)

VetRepository.findBySpecialtyName uses a bound `:specialtyName` JPQL parameter with an EXISTS subquery (avoids row duplication and specialty-collection truncation) and carries no `@Cacheable`, consistent with the two recorded ADRs it cites in its Javadoc (src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet/VetRepository.java:60-72)

No coined synonyms for ubiquitous-language terms were introduced by the new names (narrowsTheDirectory, findBySpecialtyName, specialty) — checked by reading the diff's identifiers against docs/ubiquitous-language.md's veterinarian/specialty entries
`./gradlew checkFormat` and `./gradlew compileJava` both succeed on the working tree (commands run directly)

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: The URL-encoding of the echoed specialty is correct by construction, but no test pins it: the VetControllerTests additions exercise only SPECIALTY = "radiology". A pagination-link case with a hostile value (for example `a&page=9"><script>`) asserting the encoded `specialty=` parameter would guard the designed threat-model mitigation against a regression to string-built link text.
approved_aspects: SQL injection: the new specialty filter reaches the database only as a bound JPQL named parameter, VetRepository.java `WHERE holder = vet AND LOWER(specialty.name) = LOWER(:specialtyName))` with `@Param("specialtyName") String specialtyName`. No query text is built from request input anywhere in the diff (read of the full src/main diff).

Template injection / XSS: the echoed specialty enters vetList.html only as a link-expression parameter, e.g. `th:href="${filtered} ? @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})} : @{/vets.html(page=${i})}"`, which Thymeleaf URL-encodes and attribute-escapes. The diff also removes the old `__${i}__` preprocessing from vetList.html (`grep -rn -F -e '__${' src/main/resources/templates/` finds no vets/vetList.html line; the remaining hits are pre-existing and carry server-side values such as owner.id and fragment names, not request text). No `th:utext` appears in any template (`grep -rn -F -e 'utext' src/main/resources/templates/` exits 1). The fragments do not read the new `specialty` model attribute (`grep -rn -F -e 'specialty' src/main/resources/templates/fragments/` exits 1), and the table's `th:each="specialty : ${vet.specialties}"` local is scoped to the table, not the pagination div.

Resource exhaustion: findBySpecialtyName carries no @Cacheable, so caller-chosen text never becomes a key in the unbounded `vets` cache. This matches the ADR 2026-09-13-uncached-reads-keyed-by-caller-text and the designed threat-model row in system-design.md. The JSON route's `Pageable.unpaged()` read is bounded by the vet table, the same reach as the pre-existing unfiltered `findAll()` on that route.

Binding / mass assignment: the new input is a single optional `@RequestParam String specialty` on both routes, not an object bind, so no identifier or field-binding surface is added. A blank value falls back to the full directory via `StringUtils.hasText`. No existing check (the @Cacheable on findAll, the binder disallow-lists, escaping) is removed or weakened in the diff.

Error handling and logging: the diff adds no exception message, no log statement, and no System.out (read of the src/main diff), so nothing new reaches the error page that renders exception messages (a known defect).

Secrets: `scripts/changeset.sh | grep -E '^\+' | grep -i -E 'password|secret|token|apikey|api_key|credential|private.?key'` returns one hit, the Security Context prose in docs/system-design.md mentioning datasource credentials. No credential value is added.

Supply chain: build.gradle is not in the change set and no dependency changes. `./gradlew dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath` resolves Spring Boot 4.1.1, spring-webmvc 7.0.9, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, jackson-databind (tools.jackson.core) 3.1.5 and hibernate-core 7.4.5.Final. The NVD match was not run because no dependencyCheckAnalyze plugin is configured (`grep -n -i -E 'dependencycheck|owasp' build.gradle` exits 1).

author: test-reviewer
approved_aspects: Placement is correct: the case-fold matching rule lives in VetRepository.findBySpecialtyName (JPQL, src/main/java/.../vet/VetRepository.java:29-43) and is exercised only at integration level across all three vendors — VetDirectoryFilterIntegrationTests (H2), MySqlIntegrationTests.theSpecialtyFilterShouldMatchALetterCaseVariantOnMySql, PostgresIntegrationTests.theSpecialtyFilterShouldMatchALetterCaseVariantOnPostgres — matching the ADR 2026-09-13-case-insensitive-matching-in-the-query.md decision to fold case in the query rather than the column; this rule cannot be unit-tested below a real database, so integration placement is correct per testing-principles.md § Test Pyramid.

The blank/absent-specialty normalization (VetController.narrowsTheDirectory, src/main/java/.../vet/VetController.java:89-92) is boundary-layer request normalization per system-design.md's VetController row, and is tested at that layer via VetDirectoryFilterIntegrationTests.theSpecialtyFilterShouldBeIgnoredWhenBlank (@ParameterizedTest over EMPTY and WHITESPACE_ONLY) — correct per testing-principles.md's carve-out for request binding/normalization rules.
python3 scripts/grading.py coverage-map --feature REQ-VET-003 reports all 7 Done-when bullets covered and 8 of 8 declared tests present by name in the diff's test files.

All 3 new PRD edge cases for the Veterinarian directory (specialty-holding-vet listed once with every specialty; a vet holding no specialty never matches, including the word shown for 'none') are covered: theSpecialtyFilterShouldListAVetWithSeveralSpecialtiesOnceWithAllOfThem and theSpecialtyFilterShouldNeverMatchAVetHoldingNoSpecialty in VetDirectoryFilterIntegrationTests.java.

Fixture data used in assertions (RADIOLOGISTS = Helen Leary + Henry Stevens; LINDA_DOUGLAS holding dentistry+surgery) matches the actual seed rows in src/main/resources/db/h2/data.sql:1-15 (vet_specialties rows (2,1) and (5,1) for radiology; (3,2),(3,3) for Linda Douglas) — expectations are grounded in real fixture data, not invented.
No JUnit assertEquals/assertTrue/assertFalse found in the changed test files (grep -F checked); AssertJ used throughout with whole-object comparison via the test-owned ListedVet record.

New tests follow the BDD the{Subject}Should{Outcome} naming school (theVetDirectoryShouldListOnlyVetsHoldingTheNamedSpecialty, theSpecialtyFilterShouldMatchTheWholeNameIgnoringCase, etc.) and reuse the host file's existing conventions (james()/helen() factories in VetControllerTests) where the brief is silent.

Mocking stays within policy: VetControllerTests continues the pre-existing @MockitoBean(VetRepository) + MockMvc pattern (sanctioned web-boundary double); VetDirectoryFilterIntegrationTests and the MySql/Postgres tests use real Spring context and real databases, no new mock-framework usage introduced.
./gradlew test --tests "org.springframework.samples.petclinic.vet.*" passes with the new tests (dynamic run, this review).

semantic_surprise.note: I read every prod hunk and found nothing that surprises. The blank-to-absent guard is StringUtils.hasText, applied the same way on both routes. pageRequest keeps page size 5 and the page-1 offset. The JPQL binds :specialtyName and applies LOWER to both sides inside an EXISTS self-join, so each vet appears once and keeps all its specialties. The template swaps string-built '__${i}__' hrefs for link-expression parameters, and unfiltered links come out byte-identical. One mechanism is unusual: the pageLink fragment sits outside <body>, and only the layout's th:replace keeps it from rendering in place. It is commented, and a stray render would break the containsOnly link assertions. A padded value like ' radiology' matches nothing rather than being trimmed. That is the narrow reading, and the PRD records it as an open question.

test_adequacy.note: The tests check real outcomes against the seeded H2 database through both routes. They cover whole-name matching, upper and mixed case, a prefix that must miss, a specialty nobody holds, the multi-specialty vet appearing once with every specialty, and the word shown for no specialty. Blank and whitespace-only requests are compared byte-for-byte with the unfiltered response. The H2 specialty column is case-sensitive, so the case-variant cases prove the query-side fold works. The MockMvc pagination tests assert the exact link sets, filtered and unfiltered. Remaining gaps: no hostile-value encoding case, and the MySQL/Postgres case tests need Docker, so the green build does not show they ran.

reviewer_hedging.note: All reviewers approved, but with reservations. The round-1 security approval left a recommendation: nothing tests the URL encoding of the echoed specialty against a hostile value. Its XSS evidence quoted the per-anchor th:href ternary, and the fix round then rewrote exactly those security-surface lines into the pageLink fragment. The fix-delta roster (code-quality, doc) left security out, so no security reviewer read the new form. It still passes the value only as an encoded link parameter. Also, the test-reviewer cites VetRepository.java:29-43 for the JPQL, but those lines are the interface Javadoc; the query is at lines 73-81.

scope_deviation.note: No design revisions, consultations, or build retries. The diff matches the intake exactly: an optional specialty parameter on both routes, whole-name case-insensitive matching, blank treated as absent, pagination links that carry the parameter, and no form control. NG-9 is narrowed with a non-goal ADR, and REQ-VET-004 is minted while REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn, both as the owner directed. Open questions such as trimming and narrowing by name are recorded, not decided. The fix-round delta is a template refactor, and tests show the links it produces are unchanged.

rationale: The code reads clean and in scope, and the tests pin every rule. The flag is the review trail: the fix round rewrote the security-surface pagination hrefs with no security re-review, the security approval left the encoding untested, and one test-reviewer citation is wrong. Read vetList.html:53-57 and the VetRepository query before merging.
